info.title: GTA 6 core systems and gameplay build request

messages.text:
"Role and Persona
Act as the Lead Game Director, Principal Engine Architect, and Senior AI Programmer for the RAGE (Rockstar Advanced Game Engine). Your objective is to architect the core systems, game loop, and narrative structures for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6). You will provide detailed C++ engine logic, system design documents, and backend architecture blueprints based on the following master specification.
​1. World and Environment
​Setting: The state of Leonida, featuring a sprawling, highly dense recreation of Vice City and surrounding areas like Port Gellhorn and the Leonida Keys.
​Dynamic Weather @COMMENT_BODY@ Physics: Implement a volumetric cloud system and advanced weather events, including tropical storms and hurricanes. Rain must create persistent puddles, and wind physics must dynamically affect vegetation, debris, and character hair.  
​Density @COMMENT_BODY@ Navigation: Roads are approximately 15% narrower than previous iterations to realistically simulate rush-hour traffic density. Parallax mapping must be used to simulate 3D interiors for buildings when viewed from the outside.  
​2. Protagonists @COMMENT_BODY@ Narrative Dynamics
​Dual Protagonists: The narrative centers on a Bonnie-and-Clyde dynamic between Jason Duval (an ex-military drug runner) and Lucia Caminos (a fighter recently released from prison).
​Relationship System: Code a bond system where shared activities (such as going to the gym, shopping, or playing pool) strengthen their relationship.
​Co-op Mechanics: Implement real-time role swapping, allowing players to switch seats dynamically during car chases so one can drive while the other shoots.  
​3. Core Gameplay Systems
​Combat: Remove default auto-aim. Implement a \"Focus\" ability that slows time and highlights enemy weak points, similar to Dead Eye. Enforce heavy weapon weight and recoil to make sustained fire difficult, and restrict players to a visually accurate, limited weapon loadout UI.  
​Vehicle Mechanics:
​Fuel System: Vehicles consume fuel and must be refueled at gas stations (which also repair damage) or charging stations for EVs.  
​Trunk Inventory: Every personal vehicle must have a fully functional trunk to store weapons, duffel bags, or hide NPCs/bodies.
​Stealing @COMMENT_BODY@ Hijacking: Introduce a lockpicking minigame for parked cars that can trigger alarms, and active quick-time events for hijacking where drivers or passengers may fight back.  
​Crime @COMMENT_BODY@ Heat System: Overhaul the wanted level. Crimes no longer trigger automatic police alerts. Implement a \"Heat\" system where solid white stars denote direct visual contact by law enforcement. Ensure buildings have multiple exits to support dynamic escape routing.  
​Economy: Separate player funds into three distinct pools: a secure Bank Balance (managed via the in-game BuckMe app), physical Cash (which is lost upon death or arrest), and Loot carried in duffel bags that must be fenced. Implement a Criminal Profile System that tracks player violence to dictate NPC hostility and police severity.
​4. Technical Architecture
​Performance Targets: Optimize the engine to target 1440p at 30 FPS on base current-gen consoles, utilizing Ray-Traced Global Illumination (RTGI) and ray-traced shadows.
​Backend Infrastructure: Design an event-driven microservices architecture using tools like Kafka or RabbitMQ to handle real-time matchmaking, live events, and instant relay of in-game triggers (like police chases or car crashes) across millions of concurrent users.  
​AI Behaviors: Use reinforcement learning and behavior trees for dynamic NPC responses. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
